title: Load Combination Envelope
statement: caseResults has one row per load case and one column per station along a member, holding that case's result at that station. factors has one row per load combination and one entry per load case. A combination's result at a station is the sum over load cases of factor times that case's value there. Return [maxEnvelope, minEnvelope]: two rows, each with one entry per station, giving the largest and smallest value any combination produces there.
constraints: every row of factors has exactly one entry per load case
factors may be negative, and the envelope is taken per station independently
hints: The envelope is taken station by station. The combination that governs at one station need not govern at any other, so you cannot pick a single worst combination up front.
Three nested loops do it: for each combination, for each station, sum over the load cases. Track a running max and min per station rather than storing every combination.

Seed the running max and min from the FIRST combination, not from zero. A set of combinations that are all negative would otherwise report a maximum of zero, which is the kind of bug that quietly under-designs something.
complexity: O(combinations * stations * cases) time, O(stations) extra space

cases.name: uplift: a negative factor governs the minimum
a single combination is its own envelope
different combinations govern at different stations
